scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user reboots their PC and now cannot get an IP address. Other
PCs that were already up keep working (their existing leases are
still valid). Newly connected devices on any internal VLAN time
out waiting for DHCP. Existing TCP sessions are unaffected.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 dhcpd (ISC DHCP server)
Mechanism: r1 is the central DHCP server for every internal
  VLAN (A-PC, A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi).
  DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as unicast to 10.0.0.76 (R1's
  loopback). With dhcpd dead, requests reach r1 but get no
  reply. Existing leases keep working until their lifetime
  expires; renewals start failing after lease-time/2.
Localization: r1
Root cause: dhcpd is not running on r1
Fix: restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The `isc-dhcp-server` daemon (`dhcpd`) on device `r1`, which acts as the centralized DHCP server for all internal VLANs in this enterprise topology.

**Mechanism:** DHCP lease acquisition is a four-step exchange (DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK). When a host boots or reconnects, it broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER; the distribution switches relay it to `r1`, which must respond with a DHCPOFFER. With `dhcpd` not running on `r1`, no OFFER is ever sent, so new clients time out. Hosts that already have a valid lease do not need a server response until their lease expires — their IP stack continues working purely from the cached lease, which explains why rebooted machines fail while machines that stayed up continue to work.

**Localization:** `r1` holds a fully configured `/etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf` covering every internal subnet (A-PC 10.1.0.0/24, A-Phone 10.2.0.0/24, B-PC 10.3.0.0/24, B-Phone 10.4.0.0/24, Wi-Fi 10.6.0.0/24, and both management subnets), and is configured to listen on `eth0`/`eth1` (the WAN links connecting to `csw1`/`csw2`). The OSPF routing fabric is fully healthy with 32 routes on all distribution and core switches; the relay path to `r1` is intact.

**Root cause:** The `isc-dhcp-server` daemon is down on `r1` — `pgrep -a dhcpd` returns empty and `systemctl is-active` reports `inactive` — so no new DHCP leases can be issued on any internal VLAN.

**Fix:** Restart the DHCP daemon on `r1`: `systemctl start isc-dhcp-server` (or `service isc-dhcp-server start`). New DHCP DISCOVER packets from any VLAN relay will immediately receive OFFER responses and hosts will obtain IPs.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names r1 as the affected device hosting the isc-dhcp-server (dhcpd).
The submission explicitly identifies the isc-dhcp-server (dhcpd) on r1 as the affected component and states it is not running.
The report explicitly contrasts new clients timing out with existing hosts continuing to operate from cached leases and explains why rebooted machines fail while up hosts keep working.
Recommends restarting/starting the isc-dhcp-server on r1 (systemctl/service start), which matches the expected fix to bring dhcpd back up.

The agent's investigation logs explicitly show dhcpd is not running on r1 while r1 has a full dhcpd.conf and the network/OSPF fabric is healthy; the writeup's claims follow directly from those observations and the recommended fix addresses the confirmed root cause.
